results.title: Online Ordering Portal Still Shows Menu Item as Available After Overnight Menu Sync
results.system_area: POS to online ordering platform integration (menu sync)
results.ground_truth_scope: Functional tests on POS status change behavior; integration tests on POS-to-portal sync; smoke test on online ordering checkout flow; regression on other menu item availability states.

functional_tests: Verify that marking an item as Out of Stock on the POS immediately updates its status on the POS.

Verify that removing the Out of Stock flag on the POS makes the item visible and orderable on the online web ordering app.
Verify that removing the Out of Stock flag on the POS makes the item visible and orderable on the mobile ordering app.
smoke_tests: Verify that other menu items not marked as Out of Stock remain orderable on the online ordering platform.
Check that the online ordering platform is accessible and functional after the sync process.
regression_tests: Test that the menu sync process does not affect the pricing of items on the online ordering platform.
Verify that the sync process does not alter item descriptions on the online ordering platform.
Ensure that the sync process does not affect the availability of items that are in stock.
integration_tests: Validate the end-to-end data flow from the POS to the online ordering platform for an item marked as Out of Stock.
Test the data flow when the Out of Stock status is removed, ensuring the item becomes available again on the online platform.
exploratory_tests: Test the behavior when multiple items are marked as Out of Stock simultaneously and verify their status on the online platform.
Check the system's behavior if the sync interval is manually triggered multiple times in quick succession.

coverage_depth.justification: The change is a bug fix in a critical integration area affecting customer experience, requiring thorough validation of the sync process and its impact on item availability.

effort_estimate.notes: The estimate includes tests for both web and mobile platforms, covering functional, smoke, regression, and integration scenarios. The complexity of the sync process and its impact on customer-facing systems drive the test case count.

results.title: POS Crew Notification Feature Enablement on POS Workstations
results.change_type: New feature (POS notification scheduling and display system)
results.system_area: POS workstation, employee clock-in workflow, notification management
results.ground_truth_scope: Functional test of notification creation and scheduling by a manager role; functional test of notification display on POS workstation at crew member clock-in; validation of notification content accuracy; regression on clock-in workflow to confirm no disruption; exploratory testing on edge cases such as multiple active notifications, expired notifications, and no notification scheduled.

functional_tests: Verify that notifications can be scheduled by store owners and managers.
Check that notifications appear on the POS workstation screen when a crew member clocks in.
Ensure notifications can be customized for different types of messages (promotions, policy changes, etc.).
Test the ability to schedule notifications for specific dates and times.
Validate that notifications are displayed correctly across different POS workstation models.
smoke_tests: Confirm that the POS workstation operates normally after the feature is enabled.
Verify that the clock-in process is not disrupted by the new notification feature.
regression_tests: Test existing clock-in workflows to ensure they are unaffected.
Check that existing POS functionalities (e.g., transaction processing, receipt printing) remain operational.
Validate that the notification management system does not interfere with existing POS system settings.
integration_tests: Verify integration between the POS notification system and the employee clock-in system.
Test data flow from the notification management system to the POS workstations.
Ensure that notifications are correctly synchronized across multiple POS workstations in the same store.
exploratory_tests: Test the behavior of the notification system when multiple crew members clock in simultaneously.
Check how the system handles overlapping notifications scheduled for the same time.
Explore the system's response to invalid or corrupted notification data.
